query: Single-phase high-entropy alloys have difficulty achieving a satisfactory strength–ductility balance. Earlier work introduced the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy with a uniform, fine lamellar structure to enable large-sized production and obtain good strength and plasticity, but its performance still falls short of industrial requirements. Its use in aircraft and spacecraft fasteners further requires stability under extreme temperature fluctuations, long-term mechanical loading, room-temperature creep, and corrosion, while relevant creep and corrosion studies remain limited by sample-size and experimental-environment constraints. Given these limitations and design requirements, what single intervention could improve the alloy’s practical performance? Present one hypothesis that specifies the intervention, causal mechanism, predicted improvement over the starting material, boundary conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a feasible experiment whose outcome could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: A low‐temperature aging treatment that precipitates coherent nano‐scale L12 intermetallics within the fcc lamellae of the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high‐entropy alloy will enhance its resistance to room-temperature creep, high-temperature fluctuations, and corrosion while improving overall strength without a significant loss of ductility.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high‐entropy alloy with a uniform, fine lamellar structure exhibiting limited strength–ductility balance and moderate creep and corrosion performance.
generation.intervention: Subject the alloy to a low‐temperature aging heat treatment to induce in-situ precipitation of coherent L12 nano-scale intermetallic phases within the fcc lamellae.
generation.conditions: Heat treatment at approximately 600°C for 10–20 hours under an inert atmosphere to control precipitate size and distribution.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a uniform dispersion of nanoscale, coherent L12 precipitates within the soft fcc phase.
generation.mechanism: The precipitated L12 nanoparticles obstruct dislocation motion (via mechanisms such as Orowan bowing) and stabilize the microstructure by impeding grain boundary sliding, thereby enhancing yield strength and creep resistance and improving microstructural stability under thermal fluctuations and corrosive environments.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved yield strength, reduced room-temperature creep rate, enhanced performance stability under extreme thermal cycling, and better corrosion resistance compared to the untreated alloy—all while maintaining an acceptable ductility.
generation.baseline: Performance of the current as-cast, fine lamellar AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy, which does not fully meet aerospace requirements due to limited strength–ductility balance and insufficient resistance to creep, thermal fluctuations, and corrosion.
generation.boundary: The treatment is expected to be effective within the specified temperature and time window for this eutectic HEA; over-aging or deviations from controlled conditions might lead to precipitate coarsening, which could compromise ductility and negate the improvements.
generation.uncertainty: Optimal precipitate size, volume fraction, and distribution for the best balance of mechanical and environmental properties remain uncertain; additional experiments are needed to assess long-term creep under variable temperature conditions and the impact on corrosion performance.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare multiple batches of the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy. Subject them to the aging treatment at 600°C for different durations (e.g., 10, 15, and 20 hours) and compare with untreated control samples. Use transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and X-ray diffraction (XRD) to verify the formation, coherence, and size distribution of L12 precipitates. Conduct tensile tests, creep tests under room temperature and elevated temperatures, and electrochemical corrosion tests to compare the performance.
measurements: Nano-scale precipitate identification and coherence using TEM and XRD
Mechanical properties: yield strength, tensile ductility, and creep rate
Environmental performance: corrosion resistance via electrochemical measurements
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the aging treatment fails to produce a high density of coherent L12 precipitates, or if the treated samples do not exhibit statistically significant improvements in yield strength, creep resistance, and corrosion performance compared to the control, the hypothesis will be falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Many studies [,] have shown that the precipitation strengthening by a coherent L12 phase may be an ideal method for enhancing the strength of FCC-structured H/MEAs without the excessive expense of ductility. For example, Zhao et al. [] produced a L12 phase-strengthened CoCrNi-based MEA by alloying Al and Ti elements, which exhibited a decent yield strength of 750 MPa with excellent plasticity of 45%. Wang et al. [] reported a similar (CoCrNi)94Al3Ti3 MEA, strengthened by a L12 phase, with a yield strength of 900 MPa and a fracture strain of 22.9%. In these studies [,,,], the L12 phase usually co-exists in both intergranular and intragranular forms, as a result of discontinuous and continuous precipitations, respectively. It was revealed [,] that the intragranular L12 generally precipitates at a high-density and nano-size, which not only enhances strength by hindering dislocation motion, but also allows the dislocations that shear through them to maintain plasticity.

Recent studies indicate that eutectic high-entropy alloys can simultaneously possess high strength and high ductility, which have potential industrial applications. The present study focuses on Al0.7CoCrFeNi, a lamellar dual-phase (fcc + B2) precipitation-strengthenable eutectic high entropy alloy. This alloy exhibits an fcc + B2 (B2 with bcc nano-precipitates) microstructure resulting in a combination of the soft and ductile fcc phase together with hard B2 phase. Low temperature annealing leads to the precipitation of ordered L12 intermetallic precipitates within the fcc resulting in enhanced strength. The strengthening contribution due to fine scale L12 is modeled using Orowan dislocation bowing and by-pass mechanism. The alloy was tested under quasi-static (strain-rate = 10−3 s−1) tensile loading and dynamic (strain-rate = 103 s−1) compressive loading. Due to the fine lamellar microstructure with a large number of fcc-bcc interfaces, the alloy show relatively high flow-stresses, ~1400 MPa under quasi-static loading and in excess of 1800 MPa under dynamic loading. In the present study, the effect of annealing on the microstructural and mechanical properties of HPT processed CoCrNi HEA was investigated. The results clearly indicate that the initial microstructure plays an important role in the mechanical properties of CoCrNi alloy. The initial microstructure with fine grain size of ~660 nm, high fraction of low angle grain boundaries, and high KAM value shows strain softening followed by strain hardening, whereas only strain hardening is observed for the microstructure with grain size >900 nm, a low fraction of low-angle grain boundaries, and low KAM value. The sample annealed at 700 °C for 15 min shows the optimized room temperature mechanical properties with a remarkable combination of strength (1090 MPa) and strain to failure (41%). Thus, the present study demonstrates that the severe plastic deformation followed by annealing is one of the effective ways of enhancing the mechanical properties in CoCrNi MEA.

proposals.intervention: Low‐temperature aging treatment to induce coherent nano‐scale L12 precipitation within the soft fcc lamellae
proposals.conditions: Heat treatment at approximately 600°C for 10–20 hours under an inert atmosphere
proposals.structural_mediator: Nanoscale, coherent L12 intermetallic precipitates distributed within the fcc phase
proposals.mechanism: The precipitation of L12 particles impedes dislocation motion via the Orowan bowing mechanism, enhancing yield strength and creep resistance without significantly compromising ductility; improved thermal stability of the precipitates is also expected to bolster performance under temperature fluctuations
proposals.predicted_outcome: A marked increase in strength and creep resistance with minimal loss of ductility, and enhanced microstructural stability against high‐temperature and long‐term mechanical loading compared to the as‐cast lamellar alloy
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: This single heat‐treatment intervention restructures the alloy at the nanoscale to achieve a superior strength–ductility balance and improved resistance to creep and corrosion, meeting the stringent requirements for aerospace fasteners

proposals.material_system: Modified AlCoCrFeNi2.1 high‐entropy alloy with minor Cr enrichment
proposals.intervention: Slight compositional adjustment by introducing a small additional fraction of Cr during alloy synthesis
proposals.conditions: Casting under controlled conditions with an extra 0.3–0.5 atomic fraction of Cr, followed by standard solidification and cooling
proposals.structural_mediator: A controlled microstructure transition from a uniform lamellar arrangement to a slightly dendritic–interdendritic structure that promotes beneficial phase boundary characteristics
proposals.mechanism: The increased Cr content facilitates the formation of a robust, protective passive oxide film on the alloy surface that improves corrosion resistance and positively influences creep performance; additionally, the modified phase morphology can contribute to better load transfer and stress distribution
proposals.predicted_outcome: Enhanced corrosion resistance and improved stability under long-term mechanical loading, with a concomitant strengthening effect that does not severely impact ductility
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: By tailoring the composition with a minimal Cr addition, the alloy’s surface reactivity is controlled to form protective layers, addressing both creep and corrosion challenges required for aerospace components

proposals.intervention: Interstitial doping with non-metal atoms (e.g., nitrogen) via a controlled gas-phase nitriding process
proposals.conditions: Exposure to a nitrogen-rich atmosphere at moderate temperatures (around 500–600°C) for several hours, ensuring controlled interstitial uptake
proposals.structural_mediator: Formation of finely dispersed, nano-scale nitride precipitates that promote localized chemical order within the lamellar fcc phase
proposals.mechanism: The interstitial nitrogen atoms encourage local chemical ordering and minor nitride precipitation, which hinder dislocation motion and grain boundary sliding during creep, while simultaneously stabilizing the microstructure for superior resistance to temperature fluctuations and corrosion
proposals.predicted_outcome: An overall improvement in high-temperature stability, room-temperature creep resistance, and corrosion performance with a better strength–ductility combination compared to the untreated alloy
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: This intervention directly targets multiple performance aspects—mechanical loading, creep, thermal fluctuations, and corrosion—through a single doping process that introduces beneficial local chemical order and precipitates

proposals.intervention: Application of severe plastic deformation (e.g., high-pressure torsion) followed by a controlled low-temperature anneal
proposals.conditions: Deformation at room temperature via high-pressure torsion (typically 6 revolutions) followed by annealing at 400–500°C for 1–2 hours to relieve excessive internal stresses while maintaining refined microstructure
proposals.structural_mediator: An ultrafine lamellar structure with significantly reduced grain size and enhanced density of phase boundaries
proposals.mechanism: The severe deformation refines the microstructure, increasing the density of grain boundaries and lamellar interfaces, which serve as obstacles to dislocation motion and sites for stress redistribution; the subsequent annealing relieves excessive strain while preserving the beneficial refined microstructure
proposals.predicted_outcome: Superior strength–ductility balance along with enhanced resistance to room-temperature creep and improved long-term mechanical performance under extreme thermal fluctuations and corrosive environments
proposals.why_it_addresses_the_question: This processing intervention refines the microstructure to optimize both mechanical properties and environmental resistance, meeting industrial requirements for strength, ductility, creep, and corrosion under extreme conditions

decision.rationale: Low‐temperature aging to induce nano‐scale coherent L12 precipitation in the fcc lamellae is directly aimed at enhancing both strength and creep resistance by hindering dislocation motion via the Orowan mechanism while preserving ductility. Prior studies in similar HEAs have shown that the precipitation of an L12 phase improves yield strength and thermal stability. This approach directly targets the limitations of the as‐cast lamellar microstructure and complies with the stringent requirements for aerospace fasteners under extreme temperature fluctuations and corrosive conditions.
